exemptions.test_a_new_text_already_present_elsewher: A precondition assertion about the test's OWN fixture, not about the subject. No mutation of `_lint.py` can redden it, and mutating the fixture to break its own premise would be circular — the premise exists precisely so the case cannot pass while silently testing nothing. It earned its keep on the first run: the fixture had the two branches at different indents, so the regression pin was not exercising the shape it names, and this assertion is what said so.
Same fixture-premise role as the line above; same reason it is unreachable from a mutation of the subject.

probes.name: P1-the-lint-accuses-a-healthy-battery
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: 🔴 The OVER-REFUSAL direction, which is the one that actually bit at s288. A healthy anchor resolves exactly once, so inverting the expected count makes the lint accuse every correct battery in the repo. A guard that refuses everything passes every 'does it catch X?' probe below; only this one can tell strict from broken.

probes.name: P2-probe-count-is-not-measured
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: The report prints counts so a disagreement is one step to diagnose (§8: never a bare PASS/FAIL). A count that is always zero would make every report unreadable while the verdict stayed correct — invisible to any test that checks only findings.

probes.name: P3-claim-source-count-is-not-measured
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: Sibling of P2 for the other printed count.

probes.name: P4-THE-REGRESSION-the-s288-over-refusal-restored
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: 🔴 THE probe of this battery: it restores the exact bug the first draft shipped — treating a `new` text that appears anywhere in the subject as proof the mutation is a no-op. It reported 8 of 21 batteries dead when the true number was 2, accusing six healthy ones. The fixture's two branches sit at the SAME indent so this mutation genuinely fires; if that ever drifts, the premise assertions this battery exempts are what will say so.

probes.name: P5-a-vanished-anchor-is-not-reported
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: The s287 R17 death, restored: the code moved, the battery did not, and nothing said so. Distinct from P1 in direction — P1 over-refuses, this under-refuses — and the same anchor carries both because the branch is the single decision point.

probes.name: P6-a-repeated-anchor-is-not-reported
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: The other half of 'exactly once': an anchor whose blast radius is larger than the probe declared. Pinning `hits` to 1 rather than disabling the branch keeps P5's claim green under this mutation, so the red is attributable to the counting and not to the reporting.

probes.name: P7-a-byte-identical-mutation-is-not-reported
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: The only offline-decidable no-op. Aimed at the same branch P4 aims at, from the opposite direction: P4 makes it fire too often, this makes it never fire.

probes.name: P8-an-unaddressable-claim-key-is-not-reported
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.expect_claim: test_a_claim_key_that_addresses_nothing_is_found|"does not exist in the claim sources" in details|#0
probes.note: The s287 AC-1 / AC-2 death: `ruff format` reflowed an asserted literal and stable_key is built from those bytes, so the declared key addressed nothing. The driver already refuses this — the defect was that it only refuses when somebody RUNS the battery.

probes.name: P9-an-orphan-exemption-is-not-reported
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: The third address that rots, and the one the driver reports only mid-run as 'stale ids'. An exemption is a written promise that a claim is unreachable; when the claim disappears the promise still reads as deliberate coverage while covering nothing. Found live at s288 in plan-0120-step1-db-guard.

probes.name: P10-a-missing-node-module-is-not-reported
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.expect_claim: test_a_node_id_naming_a_missing_module_is_found|"node_id names a module that does not exist" in details|#0
probes.note: A probe pointing at a test module that moved. Only the FILE is checked — resolving the test itself needs collection, which this lint deliberately does not do.

probes.name: P11-a-missing-claim-source-reports-more-than-once
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: The 'reported ALONE' half. Every later check derives from an index that cannot be built, so a missing source that also emitted a cascade of derived complaints would bury the one finding that matters. Duplicating it is the cheapest way to redden the count without touching the message P12 owns.

probes.name: P12-a-missing-claim-source-is-not-named-as-such
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: The message half. Under this mutation the COUNT stays 1, so P11's claim stays green — that green is what attributes this red to the wording rather than to a cascade.

probes.name: P13-unreadable-json-reports-more-than-once
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: A broken battery must be a FINDING, not a crash that takes the whole 21-battery run down with it. The count half.

probes.name: P14-unreadable-json-is-not-named-as-such
probes.subject: tools/probe_battery/_lint.py
probes.note: The message half. The word `unreadable` also appears in the subject-unreadable finding further down, so this anchor is the whole return line rather than the word — an anchor that matched twice would edit a site the probe never declared.
